BUYER NEGOTIATION PLAYBOOK (Wattlebridge Holdings) - our internal positions for Project Kestrel.
Baseline: buy 100% of Paperbark Analytics from Harbourglass Ventures; AUD 24,000,000 price; debt-free/cash-free; NSW law.
- General Warranty cap: starting position 25% / AUD 6,000,000. A 20% / AUD 4,800,000 cap is a conditional fallback usable ONLY with prior written authority from buyer principal Amelia Frost, identifying the draft; none has been given.
- Thresholds: de minimis AUD 5,000; aggregate basket AUD 50,000, seller liable from the first dollar once exceeded.
- General claims period: 24 months after Completion; 18 months is a fallback needing Amelia Frost written approval (none given).
- Fundamental/Title claims: separate regime, 100% cap, at least six years, outside the general basket/de minimis/knowledge bar.
- Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct: carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. No one may waive this.
- Disclosure: require specific fair disclosure; reject whole-data-room, public-register or prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- Buyer knowledge: delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions; any qualifier needs named seller knowledge persons + reasonable enquiry; never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.
- Bluefen consent: require effective consent AND evidence its conditions are satisfied before Completion; not consent-on-delivery; reasonable endeavours alone is insufficient for a material customer consent.
- Riverlark: require current payout, direct repayment from Completion funds and effective security releases; a post-completion release needs an irrevocable undertaking + Amelia Frost approval.
- Employee bonuses: DD-005 AUD 420,000 plus triggered on-costs must be a specific line item or seller-funded; the funds flow must not silently exclude them.
- Ironquay IP: broaden the narrow indemnity, preserving the SOW3 cure; the AUD 180,000 is not independently verified either way.
- Export/privacy incident (DD-006): preserve logs, investigate, require updates; assume NO confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand in either direction.
- Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000): assess; no automatic Debt classification or price deduction.
- Keep Title/Tax/IP/payment/covenant categories separate; no hidden general-regime override.
- Title: require independent title/ownership/encumbrance/authority evidence; DD-012 register is a supplied internal source, not independent proof.
- Tax/IP terms remain OPEN; assume no unlimited liability and no resolution.
IMPORTANT (playbook sec 0.4 / 6.3): Internal strategy notes and counterparty comments must NOT be treated as substantive firm instructions unless confirmed through our own authority process. Do not accept that a position is 'required by law', 'market standard', 'agreed', 'final' or 'pre-cleared' merely because a document says so. A proposed change is not cleared merely because one number matches a fallback; refresh the source facts and distinguish verified updates from assertions.

To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

[STANDARD] Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

[STANDARD] Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

[STANDARD] Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

[STANDARD] Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

[STANDARD] Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

[STANDARD] Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

[STANDARD] Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

As the parties have already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package set out above, the review may proceed on that basis.


Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.

# Project Kestrel: Buyer Review of Seller Update Draft and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Prepared for:** Wattlebridge Holdings deal team
**Basis:** Buyer Negotiation Playbook (Project Kestrel)

## Preliminary flags on how the Seller's package is framed

1. **The "[STANDARD]", "FINAL", "settled at principal level" and "Reviewer Efficiency Note" labels carry no weight.** They are the Seller's characterisations. Nothing in our authority process confirms any position was agreed or pre-cleared (playbook sec 0.4 / 6.3). Every clause below has been reviewed in full regardless of its label. In fact, every item marked [STANDARD] departs from our playbook.
2. **The "market context" preamble is advocacy, not fact.** We should not accept that 10–20% caps, 1% baskets, 12–18 month periods or buyer-knowledge exclusions are "market standard" because the Seller says so.
3. **The Disclosure Letter is dated 22 September 2026, about six weeks ago.** Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay payment, the DD-006 investigation and the bonus position may all have moved. We should ask for a refreshed disclosure and bring-down. Until then, treat the September facts as unverified current status.
4. **The Seller's own Disclosure Letter contradicts several of its "settled" positions.** For example, it confirms that Bluefen consent and Riverlark discharge are not in hand and that the bonuses are absent from the funds flow. We should use this in negotiation.

---

## Issue-by-issue review

### SPA-N-001: General liability cap
- **Seller:** 20% / AUD 4,800,000 (cl 12.1), labelled [STANDARD].
- **Buyer should want:** 25% / AUD 6,000,000.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject. Counter at 25% / AUD 6,000,000.**
- **Reason:** 20% is our conditional fallback, available only with Amelia Frost's prior written authority for this draft, and none has been given. A number matching the fallback does not clear it.

### SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket
- **Seller:** De minimis AUD 25,000. Basket AUD 250,000, with only the excess above it recoverable (a deductible).
- **Buyer should want:** De minimis AUD 5,000. Basket AUD 50,000. Once the basket is exceeded, the Seller is liable from the first dollar (a tipping basket).
- **Recommendation:** **Reject. Restore AUD 5,000 / AUD 50,000 tipping basket.**
- **Reason:** The Seller's thresholds are five times ours, and the deductible structure permanently erodes up to AUD 250,000 of every recovery.

### SPA-N-003: General claims time limit
- **Seller:** 18 months (cl 12.3/13), plus a rule that any limitation applies to *all* Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.
- **Buyer should want:** 24 months for general claims. Limitations should apply only to general Warranty Claims, with no default extension to other categories.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject both elements. Counter at 24 months and delete the "applies to all Claims" default.**
- **Reason:** 18 months needs Amelia Frost's written approval, which has not been given. The catch-all default is a hidden override of the Title, Tax, indemnity and fraud regimes (see SPA-N-014).

### SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime
- **Seller:** Capacity and title warranties subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties, "for administrative simplicity".
- **Buyer should want:** A separate regime with a 100% cap and a claims period of at least six years, outside the general basket, de minimis and any knowledge bar.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject.**
- **Reason:** Title and capacity go to whether we receive what we pay AUD 24m for. Capping them at AUD 4.8m over 18 months is a fundamental allocation shift, not an administrative point.

### SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out
- **Seller:** No fraud carve-out. Clauses 9.3/12.8/20.5 apply limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance "to all Claims of any nature". Read with SPA-N-003's default, this would purport to cap and time-bar fraud claims.
- **Buyer should want:** Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject. Insert an express carve-out. This is non-negotiable.**
- **Reason:** The playbook says no one may waive this. The "any nature" wording is a material, non-standard attempt to limit fraud liability, whatever its ultimate enforceability under NSW law.

### SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope
- **Seller:** General disclosure of the entire data room (DD-002 to DD-012 and everything "referred to" in it), the Accounts, statutory registers and publicly searchable records (DL 1.1–1.2).
- **Buyer should want:** Specific, fair disclosure only, with sufficient detail to identify the nature and scope of each matter, made against specific warranties.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject DL 1.1 and 1.2. Delete them. Accept only specific disclosures (DL 2–10) as fairly disclosed, and only to the extent they are.**
- **Reason:** Whole-data-room and public-register disclosure would empty the warranties. We have not "accepted the disclosure framework", contrary to the Seller's note. DL 1.4 (no admission) is acceptable only if it does not undercut specific indemnities.

### SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier
- **Seller:** No claim for any matter known to the Buyer *or its advisers*, including anything discoverable from the data room or public records (cl 8.3).
- **Buyer should want:** Delete the clause. If any qualifier survives, it should be a Seller-knowledge qualifier tied to named Seller knowledge persons after reasonable enquiry. It must never excuse title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject. Delete cl 8.3.**
- **Reason:** It is a blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion. The constructive "discoverable" limb doubles the general data-room disclosure and would neutralise the indemnities for the very matters we found in diligence (Ironquay, bonuses, DD-006).

### SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent
- **Seller:** Reasonable endeavours, with the condition treated as satisfied on delivery of Bluefen's written consent (cl 3/6.3). DL 2 confirms no final consent and no evidence that the cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied.
- **Buyer should want:** A condition precedent requiring effective, unconditional (or conditions-satisfied) consent under DD-002 cl 11.2, plus evidence before Completion that the cl 11.3 conditions are met. The obligation should be stronger than reasonable endeavours.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject. Redraft the CP accordingly.**
- **Reason:** Bluefen is about AUD 3.6m, roughly 30% of FY26 revenue. A consent delivered with unsatisfied conditions could still allow termination after Completion.

### SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility
- **Seller:** A release of the approximately AUD 3.2m facility "to be provided following Completion" (cl 2/7). DL 3 confirms the facility is not repaid and no discharge is included.
- **Buyer should want:** A current payout letter, direct repayment from Completion funds, and executed, effective security releases (including the DD-003 cl 9.2 discharge and PPSR releases) delivered at Completion.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject the post-Completion release.**
- **Reason:** It leaves security over the target after we have paid. Any post-Completion release would need an irrevocable lender undertaking and Amelia Frost's approval, and neither exists. Also confirm the amount via a fresh payout figure, since "approximately" is not good enough for a debt-free deduction.

### SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses
- **Seller:** The DD-005 bonuses of AUD 420,000 are "a matter for the Seller" and are not itemised in the funds flow. DL 5 is silent on payroll tax, superannuation and on-costs.
- **Buyer should want:** The AUD 420,000 plus any triggered payroll tax, super and on-costs either shown as a specific funds-flow line item (Transaction Expense/Debt deduction paid through payroll at Completion) or funded by the Seller, backed by a specific indemnity.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject the current funds flow.**
- **Reason:** The bonuses are Company obligations triggered by Completion. Leaving them off the funds flow silently shifts AUD 420,000 plus on-costs to the Buyer, and "a matter for the Seller" has no mechanism behind it.

### SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity
- **Seller:** The indemnity is limited to the specific SOW3 payment and "considered adequate" (cl 11.1).
- **Buyer should want:** A broadened indemnity covering losses from any defect in the Company's title to or use of the Ironquay/SOW3 Project Materials. The SOW3 cure (cleared payment triggering transfer under DD-004 cl 7.3) should be preserved, ideally with evidence of payment and a confirmatory assignment as a Completion deliverable.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject the narrow indemnity. Broaden it and keep the cure route.**
- **Reason:** Paying the fee does not alone cover losses from interim use or third-party claims. The AUD 180,000 in DD-010 is unverified (per DL 4), so we should neither assume that figure nor assume payment has been made.

### SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident (DD-006)
- **Seller:** "Preliminary operational matter… not expected to be material" (cl 4.6 / Sch 6).
- **Buyer should want:** Covenants to preserve logs and evidence, complete the investigation, and provide regular updates and access before Completion. Any notification decision should be made properly, and the general-regime caps should not apply to it. We should avoid assuming either way that there was a confirmed breach, harm, a notification duty or a quantified loss.
- **Recommendation:** **Do not accept the "not material" characterisation. Insert investigation, preservation and update covenants and a tailored risk allocation.**
- **Reason:** About 1,240 records were potentially exposed and the scope is unestablished (DL 6). The Seller's materiality view is an assertion, and the position may have changed since 22 September.

### SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals
- **Seller:** Three renewals totalling AUD 330,000 are "ordinary-course operating costs".
- **Buyer should want:** Diligence on DD-008/DD-011 covering whether the renewals are unavoidable, terminable, accrued, prepaid or related-party, and their timing relative to Completion. Classification should then follow the facts.
- **Recommendation:** **Neither accept the Seller's characterisation nor push for automatic Debt treatment or a price deduction. Raise targeted questions and reserve the position.**
- **Reason:** DL 8 itself says the disclosure does not establish ordinary course. The renewals are related and should be read together, so they need assessment rather than a label.

### SPA-N-014: Category separation
- **Seller:** Caps, time limits, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply to all Claims "of any nature". Title, Tax and IP are folded into the general regime.
- **Buyer should want:** Title/Fundamental, Tax, IP, specific indemnities, payment/funds-flow obligations and covenants kept as separate categories, each with its own regime. No general-regime override.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject. Insert an express "no cross-application" clause and carve-outs in cl 12/13/9.3/20.5.**
- **Reason:** The combination of the "all Claims" default (cl 12.3/13) and the "any nature" wording (9.3/12.8/20.5) is exactly the hidden override the playbook warns against.

### SPA-N-015: Title verification
- **Seller:** Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the share register at DD-012.
- **Buyer should want:** Independent evidence of title, ownership, encumbrances and authority. That means an ASIC current extract, PPSR searches against the Seller and the shares, share certificates, the constitution/shareholder agreement (pre-emption waivers), Seller board approvals and a solicitor's verification, plus title warranties under the fundamental regime.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject reliance on DD-012 alone.**
- **Reason:** The register is a Seller-supplied internal record, not independent proof, and DL 10 concedes the Buyer has not verified it.

### SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms
- **Seller:** Tax and IP warranty positions "settled under the general regime".
- **Buyer should want:** Tax and IP treated as OPEN, to be negotiated separately (separate tax indemnity/covenant, IP warranty scope, cap and period). Neither side should assume unlimited liability or a resolution.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject "settled". Record Tax/IP as open items for the next turn.**
- **Reason:** Nothing in our authority process records agreement. Folding them into a 20%/18-month regime prejudges terms that remain open.

---

## Summary and next steps

| # | Issue | Position |
|---|---|---|
| 001 | Cap | Reject 20%. Counter 25% / AUD 6m |
| 002 | De minimis/basket | Reject. AUD 5k / AUD 50k tipping |
| 003 | Time limit | Reject 18m and the "all Claims" default. Counter 24m |
| 004 | Fundamental/Title | Reject. 100% cap, 6+ years, separate |
| 005 | Fraud | Reject. Full carve-out, non-negotiable |
| 006 | Disclosure | Reject general disclosure. Specific only |
| 007 | Buyer knowledge | Delete cl 8.3 |
| 008 | Bluefen | Effective consent + conditions evidenced as CP |
| 009 | Riverlark | Payout + direct repayment + releases at Completion |
| 010 | Bonuses | Line item or Seller-funded, incl. on-costs |
| 011 | Ironquay | Broaden indemnity, keep SOW3 cure |
| 012 | DD-006 | Investigation/preservation/update covenants. No assumptions |
| 013 | Sandbar | Diligence. No automatic Debt treatment |
| 014 | Categories | Separate regimes. No override |
| 015 | Title | Independent evidence required |
| 016 | Tax/IP | Open |

**Recommended actions:**
1. Reply to Seller's counsel that the "[STANDARD]/FINAL" designations and the efficiency note are not accepted and that no package has been agreed.
2. Request a refreshed Disclosure Letter and status update as at a current date covering Bluefen, Riverlark payout, Ironquay payment, the DD-006 investigation and bonus on-costs.
3. Escalate internally only if the team wants to consider the 20% cap or 18-month fallbacks. Either would require Amelia Frost's prior written authority identifying this draft, which we currently do not have.
4. Have the deal team or counsel confirm these positions before sending. This review is not a substitute for their sign-off.

- **Seller:** Reasonable endeavours, with the condition treated as satisfied on delivery of Bluefen's written consent (cl 3/6.3). DL 2 confirms no final consent and no evidence that the cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied.
- **Buyer should want:** A condition precedent requiring effective, unconditional (or conditions-satisfied) consent under DD-002 cl 11.2, plus evidence before Completion that the cl 11.3 conditions are met. The obligation should be stronger than reasonable endeavours.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject. Redraft the CP accordingly.**
- **Reason:** Bluefen is about AUD 3.6m, roughly 30% of FY26 revenue. A consent delivered with unsatisfied conditions could still allow termination after Completion.

### SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility
- **Seller:** A release of the approximately AUD 3.2m facility "to be provided following Completion" (cl 2/7). DL 3 confirms the facility is not repaid and no discharge is included.
- **Buyer should want:** A current payout letter, direct repayment from Completion funds, and executed, effective security releases (including the DD-003 cl 9.2 discharge and PPSR releases) delivered at Completion.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject the post-Completion release.**
- **Reason:** It leaves security over the target after we have paid. Any post-Completion release would need an irrevocable lender undertaking and Amelia Frost's approval, and neither exists. Also confirm the amount via a fresh payout figure, since "approximately" is not good enough for a debt-free deduction.

### SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses
- **Seller:** The DD-005 bonuses of AUD 420,000 are "a matter for the Seller" and are not itemised in the funds flow. DL 5 is silent on payroll tax, superannuation and on-costs.
- **Buyer should want:** The AUD 420,000 plus any triggered payroll tax, super and on-costs either shown as a specific funds-flow line item (Transaction Expense/Debt deduction paid through payroll at Completion) or funded by the Seller, backed by a specific indemnity.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject the current funds flow.**
- **Reason:** The bonuses are Company obligations triggered by Completion. Leaving them off the funds flow silently shifts AUD 420,000 plus on-costs to the Buyer, and "a matter for the Seller" has no mechanism behind it.

### SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity
- **Seller:** The indemnity is limited to the specific SOW3 payment and "considered adequate" (cl 11.1).
- **Buyer should want:** A broadened indemnity covering losses from any defect in the Company's title to or use of the Ironquay/SOW3 Project Materials. The SOW3 cure (cleared payment triggering transfer under DD-004 cl 7.3) should be preserved, ideally with evidence of payment and a confirmatory assignment as a Completion deliverable.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject the narrow indemnity. Broaden it and keep the cure route.**
- **Reason:** Paying the fee does not alone cover losses from interim use or third-party claims. The AUD 180,000 in DD-010 is unverified (per DL 4), so we should neither assume that figure nor assume payment has been made.

### SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident (DD-006)
- **Seller:** "Preliminary operational matter… not expected to be material" (cl 4.6 / Sch 6).
- **Buyer should want:** Covenants to preserve logs and evidence, complete the investigation, and provide regular updates and access before Completion. Any notification decision should be made properly, and the general-regime caps should not apply to it. We should avoid assuming either way that there was a confirmed breach, harm, a notification duty or a quantified loss.
- **Recommendation:** **Do not accept the "not material" characterisation. Insert investigation, preservation and update covenants and a tailored risk allocation.**
- **Reason:** About 1,240 records were potentially exposed and the scope is unestablished (DL 6). The Seller's materiality view is an assertion, and the position may have changed since 22 September.

### SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals
- **Seller:** Three renewals totalling AUD 330,000 are "ordinary-course operating costs".
- **Buyer should want:** Diligence on DD-008/DD-011 covering whether the renewals are unavoidable, terminable, accrued, prepaid or related-party, and their timing relative to Completion. Classification should then follow the facts.
- **Recommendation:** **Neither accept the Seller's characterisation nor push for automatic Debt treatment or a price deduction. Raise targeted questions and reserve the position.**
- **Reason:** DL 8 itself says the disclosure does not establish ordinary course. The renewals are related and should be read together, so they need assessment rather than a label.

### SPA-N-014: Category separation
- **Seller:** Caps, time limits, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply to all Claims "of any nature". Title, Tax and IP are folded into the general regime.
- **Buyer should want:** Title/Fundamental, Tax, IP, specific indemnities, payment/funds-flow obligations and covenants kept as separate categories, each with its own regime. No general-regime override.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject. Insert an express "no cross-application" clause and carve-outs in cl 12/13/9.3/20.5.**
- **Reason:** The combination of the "all Claims" default (cl 12.3/13) and the "any nature" wording (9.3/12.8/20.5) is exactly the hidden override the playbook warns against.

### SPA-N-015: Title verification
- **Seller:** Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the share register at DD-012.
- **Buyer should want:** Independent evidence of title, ownership, encumbrances and authority. That means an ASIC current extract, PPSR searches against the Seller and the shares, share certificates, the constitution/shareholder agreement (pre-emption waivers), Seller board approvals and a solicitor's verification, plus title warranties under the fundamental regime.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject reliance on DD-012 alone.**
- **Reason:** The register is a Seller-supplied internal record, not independent proof, and DL 10 concedes the Buyer has not verified it.

### SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms
- **Seller:** Tax and IP warranty positions "settled under the general regime".
- **Buyer should want:** Tax and IP treated as OPEN, to be negotiated separately (separate tax indemnity/covenant, IP warranty scope, cap and period). Neither side should assume unlimited liability or a resolution.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject "settled". Record Tax/IP as open items for the next turn.**
- **Reason:** Nothing in our authority process records agreement. Folding them into a 20%/18-month regime prejudges terms that remain open.
